CLOSING OF NON-BROKERED PRIVATE PLACEMENT
Fundraise closed oversubscribed for a total investment of £1,313,000
Fundraise Shares have a restriction period ending four months from issue
Net proceeds to be used by the Company to accelerate exploration on its Irish exploration assets and for general working capital purposes
Conroy Gold and Natural Resources plc (AIM: CGNR), the gold exploration and development company focused on Ireland and Finland, announces that the Company has received all funds from investors and closed its non-brokered private placement for a total of £1,313,000 at a price of 8 pence per share (the “
Fundraise
”), the terms of which are set out in the Company’s announcement dated 29 July 2026, as updated in the announcement of 10 August 2026. The participants in the Fundraise include
both existing and new shareholders.
The Company intends to use the net proceeds from the Fundraise for further geological work on the Company's assets in Ireland, to continue with its activities in securing material asset-level investment, and for general working capital purposes.
Mr. John Sherman, the Company's Chairman, commented:
"We are delighted that the Fundraise has closed oversubscribed and I would like to thank both our existing shareholders and the new investors who have joined the register for their strong support. The level of demand, particularly from long-term value investors in North America, is a clear endorsement of the scale and quality of the Company's 'Discs of Gold' project in Ireland.
We look forward now to the next phase of exploration at Clontibret and Clay Lake and progressing with our work towards a dual listing on the TSX-Venture Exchange in Canada.”
Additional information
Conroy has conditionally raised £1,313,000, prior to expenses, through the issue of 16,412,500 new Ordinary Shares of €0.001 (“
Ordinary Shares
”) at a price of 8 pence per share (the “
Fundraise Shares
”).
An application has been made for admission of the Fundraise Shares to trading on AIM, which is expected to occur on or around 4 September 2026 (“
Admission
”).
The Fundraise has been conducted within the Company’s existing share authorities and allotment is conditional upon Admission.
Every two Fundraise Shares will be accompanied by a warrant to subscribe for one further Ordinary Share at a price of 15 pence at any time up to 31 August 2028 (the “
Warrants
”).
The Fundraise Shares, or any Ordinary Shares being issued as a result of any exercise of Warrants, are subject to a restricted or 'lock-in' period ending 4 months from the date of allotment of the Fundraise Shares.
The participants in the Fundraise are primarily long-term value investors from North America.
Of these shareholders: (i) Mr. Ryan Matthiesen has subscribed for 500,000 Fundraise Shares, increasing his overall shareholding to 6,275,000 Ordinary Shares; (ii) Mr. Lowell Schmidt has subscribed for 625,000 Fundraise Shares, increasing his overall shareholding to 3,125,000 Ordinary Shares; and (iii) Mr. Harry Pokrandt has subscribed for 1,375,000 Fundraise Shares increasing his overall shareholding to 3,125,000 Ordinary Shares. These participants in the Fundraise are expected to hold 6.72 per cent., 3.35 per cent. and 3.35 per cent. respectively of the enlarged ordinary share capital of the Company on Admission.
On Admission, and for the purposes of the FCA Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules, the Company's total issued voting share capital will consist of 93,361,933 Ordinary Shares with one voting right per ordinary share.
The above figure may be used by shareholders as the denominator for the calculations by which they will determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in, the Company, under the FCA’s Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.
About the ‘Discs of Gold’ project
Conroy’s ‘Discs of Gold’ project in
Ireland
is defined by two parallel district scale gold trends, extending over c.90km, which are 100 per cent. held under license by the Company, anchored by the Clontibret gold deposit. The Clontibret target area contains a currently defined 517Koz gold resource @ 2.0 g/t Au (320Koz Au Indicated and 197Koz Au Inferred (2017)) which remains open in multiple directions. The Company has identified a further seven gold targets in its license area with the Clay Lake and Creenkill gold targets being of particular interest.

Conroy Gold and Natural Resources plc (AIM: CGNR), the gold exploration and development company focused on Ireland and Finland, announces that it is undertaking a non-brokered private placement (the "Proposed Fundraise") to raise gross proceeds of, in aggregate, up to £0.8m from the issue of the Company’s ordinary shares of €0.001 (“Ordinary Shares”) at a price of £0.08 (the “Issue Price”) per Ordinary Share.

Conroy Gold & Natural Resources Plc - Operational and Corporate Update
Conroy Gold & Natural Resources Plc - Operational and Corporate Update
PR Newswire
LONDON, United Kingdom, July 06
6 July 2026
Conroy Gold and Natural Resources plc
("Conroy Gold" or "the Company")
OPERATIONAL AND CORPORATE UPDATE
Progress with Drilling Programme and TSX-V listing
·
Phase I drilling programme at Clontibret successfully undertaken, with five holes completed and a series of strongly encouraging assay results announced
·
Results indicate continuity both along strike and at depth, the identification of a significant Buddingtonite alteration zone, and increasing confidence in continuity between Clontibret and the Corcaskea target
·
Assay results are awaited from follow-on deep hole CGC-25-007, drilled to target the stockwork zone informed by CGC-25-001 (deepest gold mineralisation intersected to date)
·
Phase II of work has commenced, with drilling underway to test the extension of the Orlock Bridge Fault from the mineralisation in the Clay Lake target southwestwards towards the Clontibret deposit
·
The Company is continuing to advance plans for a dual listing on the TSX-Venture Exchange
Conroy Gold and Natural Resources plc (AIM: CGNR) is pleased to provide the following operational and corporate update on its "Discs of Gold" project in Ireland, anchored by the Clontibret gold deposit.
Operational Update
The Company is pleased to report the successful completion of its Phase I drilling programme at Clontibret which included the first steps towards understanding mineralisation at depth together with enhancing understanding of the Central zone lodes associated with the historic Tullybuck antimony mine and testing the continuity of the mineralising system towards the Corcaskea target.
The programme, carried out with three drill rigs, has enhanced the Company's geological understanding of the Clontibret system and reinforced its interpretation of a large, structurally controlled gold system that remains open in all directions.
The first hole of the programme, CGC-25-001, announced by the Company on 2 March 2026, intersected the deepest gold mineralisation recorded at Clontibret to date.
More than ten gold-bearing lodes were intersected with a best intercept of 2.8 metres at 4.5 g/t Au (including 0.5 metres at 15.0 g/t Au). At approximately 410 metres depth a zone of sulphide mineralisation returned 4 metres at 0.5 g/t Au.
The hole stopped in this mineralisation due to technical difficulties. The hole confirmed the interpreted continuity of mineralisation along strike and to depth.
The mineralising system remains open at depth.
These results continue to support the geological analogies between Clontibret and the high-grade Fosterville Gold Mine in Victoria, Australia (current endowment in excess of 10 million ounces) and underlines the potential for multi-million-ounce gold mineralisation at depth.
Drill holes CGC-25-002 and CGC-25-003, announced by the Company on 18 May 2026, identified a significant, intensely altered zone interpreted to represent Buddingtonite alteration - a widely recognised pathfinder mineral associated with hydrothermal gold systems that may act as an important vectoring tool towards further mineralisation at depth. Both holes also returned highly encouraging gold mineralisation across multiple zones, including headline intersections of 1.0 metre at 16.7 g/t Au and 3.5 metres at 4.8 g/t Au (including 0.5 metres at 11.2 g/t Au), as part of a step-out programme testing the northern strike extent to depth of the Central zone lodes associated with the historic Tullybuck antimony mine.
Most recently, on 22 June 2026, the Company announced results from step-out drillhole CGC-25-005 on the Eastern Zone, which increased confidence in the continuity of the mineralised system in an area of minimal drilling within the resource footprint northwards towards the Corcaskea target, where trenching has returned 16.5 metres at 6.5 g/t Au. Several of the lode zones intersected were stronger and wider than in the nearest comparable historic drillhole (CL84-1; located c.150m to the south), providing additional support for the Company's interpretation of persistent gold-bearing lodes extending northwards, and demonstrating that the deposit remains open towards the highly prospective Corcaskea target.
Drillhole CGC-25-007 targeted the stockwork zone at depth directly below the old Tullybuck antimony mine and was informed by observations from CGC-25-001. CGC-25-007 was drilled to a down hole depth of 592.1 metres at an angle of -83
o
for a true depth of 588m and represents a key step in enhancing the geological knowledge of the Clontibret gold mineralisation system and assessing the potential for higher-grade, structurally controlled mineralisation at depth. company_30s.what_they_do: CGNR Ltd is an Irish junior mining exploration firm that drills and assays gold in the Clontibret area. The company’s job is to find, prove, and build a resource estimate that could eventually lead to a mine.
company_30s.why_they_matter: Gold is a global safe‑haven, and the Clontibret region sits in a prolific part of the Irish mining district. If CGNR can confirm significant gold mineralisation, it could become a new producer that adds to the UK and Irish mining footprint.
company_30s.current_state: The firm is still in the exploration phase, has not yet generated revenue and is raising capital through private placements to fund drilling and corporate costs. It’s burning cash to keep the drill program alive while the market remains uncertain, reflected in a near‑zero share price.

rns_narrative: Capital raising and corporate updates: a £0.8m private placement and several corporate filings (broker appointment, AGM, warrants) show the company is actively seeking funds.
Exploration progress: several drill holes and step‑out intercepts have been reported, with the latest update in September 2026 highlighting new gold assays.
Governance and shareholder activity: the company has released half‑year results, voting rights, and other corporate updates that keep investors informed about ownership and regulatory compliance.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet curiosity – a small, mixed crowd that is watching but not yet convinced.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some traders point to the recent private placement and the promising drill results as signs of potential upside if the assays come back strong.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Others warn that the company has no revenue, a thin capital base, and uncertain drilling outcomes, which could leave the stock trapped at a low price.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from neutral to slightly bullish after the latest drill announcement, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat, meaning there is no public hype. A catalyst could therefore create a surprise move.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the next drill program and publication of assay results – a gold concentration above the company’s target threshold would trigger a buying frenzy.
Announcement of the final private placement close – a successful raise of the £0.8m would validate the company’s funding plan.
A clear resource estimate or a preliminary mine plan – any step toward a feasible mine could lift sentiment.
expect_next.watch_for: Positive assay figures (e.g., >5 g/t gold), a funding announcement, a volume spike that breaks the 50‑day moving average, and the share price moving above the last low (support).
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early post‑crash phase. A clear positive drill result or funding confirmation could start a mean‑reversion rally. Until then the price is likely to stay near the low.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: CGNR has a deep crash (likely >70% off its peak) and no current upside catalysts. If the next drill shows strong gold, the price could jump to the midpoint of its pre‑crash range – a 10‑20× return on the current price. The asymmetry is large because the downside is capped at the current price while the upside could be 10‑20×.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company has no revenue, a thin capital base, and uncertain drilling outcomes. If the next assay is weak, the company may need another raise that could further dilute shareholders. Worst case, the price could stay near zero or the company could be forced to halt drilling.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside 10‑20×; downside limited to the current price. Risk/reward roughly 1:10.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a positive drill assay or funding announcement. Use a tight stop 10‑15% below the support level (the last low). Size the position to 5‑10% of your portfolio to keep risk manageable.
playbook.if_watching: Hold cash or a small position until the next assay is released. If the assay exceeds the company’s target, consider a partial entry. Monitor volume – a spike above the 50‑day MA could confirm interest.
playbook.if_passing: There are no terminal risks identified (no delisting or bankruptcy filings). Therefore, if the company fails to produce positive results, the risk is limited to the current price.

ai_insights.bottom_line: CGNR is a deeply crashed junior miner with a clear exploration focus; a positive drill result or funding close could unlock a 10‑20× upside, but the risk is limited to the near‑zero current price.
